_what: OpenStreetMap geometry for SDSC (Sao Carlos / Mario Pereira Lopes) and the LATAM MRO, converted to the scene's local ENU frame. Companion to sdsc_aip_survey.json, which carries the official survey values and OVERRIDES anything here that disagrees.

_license.share_alike_note: ODbL is share-alike: a derived database (this JSON, and any mesh generated straight from it) must be published under ODbL as well.

reference_frame.type: local East-North-Up tangent plane (WGS84 -> ECEF -> ENU)

reference_frame.z_convention: All z are 0 in this file: this is a PLAN, not terrain.

latam_mro.what_it_is: LATAM MRO Sao Carlos - LATAM's heavy-maintenance base.
latam_mro.how_identified: OSM multipolygon relation/7422930, landuse=industrial, name='TAM MRO', website tammro.com.br. It is the only industrial site inside the aerodrome.
latam_mro.osm_name_warning: The SAME relation carries name:en='TAM Museum', wikidata=Q3868501 and wikipedia=pt:Museu TAM. Q3868501 is the MUSEU TAM, a separate aviation museum that shared this site and closed in 2016. The polygon is the MRO; the museum tags on it are wrong. Do not follow them.

relation_to_runway_02.note: Distances are of the site CENTRE, projected on the RWY 02 track. The block spans 1155-2095 m along the roll and 360-1407 m off the centreline.

latam_mro.osm_survey_date: 2017-07-27 - every MRO building and apron in OSM is version 1 from one tracing session by user 'naoliv' on that date, except way/708700156 (2019-07-30) and way/510750642 (2021-06-17). HANGAR 9, INAUGURATED 2025-09-26, IS THEREFORE NOT IN THIS DATA.

departure_02_landmarks.explanation: Every mapped feature projected onto the RWY 02 take-off roll. distance_along_roll_m is metres from THR 02 (the origin) along the runway; lateral_offset_m is the perpendicular distance from the centreline; side is as seen from an aircraft rolling on 02 (northbound, true 001 deg).
departure_02_landmarks.note: The whole LATAM MRO is on the RIGHT, 360-1400 m out, from 1155 m into the roll onwards - i.e. it comes abeam right around rotation and stays in frame after lift-off. The Aeroclube's GA apron and hangars are the only thing on the LEFT, and they are in the first 500 m. Departing 20 instead mirrors all of this AND puts the base behind the aircraft from the very start of the roll.
